propositions: MCP clients receive opaque -32001 transport timeout when review_plan/verify_completion runs long enough to reach LLM passes, leaving the caller unable to distinguish success from failure despite the server completing and signing the attestation
Re-invocation of review_plan/verify_completion after a -32001 timeout launches a second billable LLM review if the first run is still in-flight, multiplying cost unboundedly under retry loops

An in-process singleflight registry keyed on (gate_type, canonical_ticket_id, basis_ref, variant, readonly) prevents duplicate concurrent calls from launching separate LLM reviews and instead attaches to the in-flight run

Async start tools (review_plan_start/verify_completion_start) mirroring the shipped run_workflow pattern return a job handle in <100ms and poll completion via plan_review_status/verify_completion_status, persisting verdicts durably to the git-backed event log
A blue-green flip that kills an in-flight run costs at most one re-run (bounded), recovered via durable event-log replay without requiring cross-flip dedup infrastructure
The fix is portable (no CI-provider coupling) and accessible to MCP-only clients observing completion via event-log polls over MCP
